findings.message: The optional properties of `AnalyzeOneShotArgs` (`repo?`, `target?`, `scope?`) are declared without `| undefined`. With exactOptionalPropertyTypes on, the documented convention is to declare optional props as `| undefined`. The `AnalyzeOneShotDeps` interface in the same file (and `ResolveRepoDeps`, `StepHostOptions` and `InDaemonClientDeps` elsewhere in this change) already follows that convention, so this interface is the inconsistent one.
The inline parameter type of `oneShotRunParams` declares `target?` and `scope?` without `| undefined`, which departs from the documented optional-property convention under exactOptionalPropertyTypes.

Present but unverified: the review was not given a build record, so none of the promised tests has a confirmed pass. I could not run them either, because running the suites needs approval. All 28 automated promised tests exist by exact title: in-daemon-client.test.ts, step-context.test.ts, step-host.test.ts, workflow-rpc-imports.test.ts, forward-step.test.ts, import-graph.test.ts, sampling-retired.test.ts, mcp-process-e2e.test.ts, mcp-process-refused.test.ts, shared/review-stream.test.ts, lance live-vector-store-owner/no-live-vector-store-in-tests, and graph live-store-owner/live-store-refusal. The moved step suites also exist under src/daemon/steps/*/__tests__. A BUILD/TESTS record for s11 was committed in 2cd169d7 but did not reach this review's grounding, so do not read these as green.

The coverage evidence is empty, so it can't decide anything. All 70 changed entries are file-level diff stubs, and every testsReaching is empty, including the test files themselves and new modules that their own new tests import directly. Examples: daemon-client.ts is imported by in-daemon-client.test.ts, host.ts by step-host.test.ts, and resolve-repo.ts and analyze-oneshot.ts by step-context.test.ts. The empty testsReaching shows the graph has not been grounded yet. It does not show that the code is unexercised, so I report no HIGH not-exercised findings from it. Re-ground once the index has caught up, or judge coverage from a run of the suites.

No unit or integration test runs the daemon's real start-up wiring: installStepDaemonClient(createInDaemonClient(rpcHandlers, streamHandlers)) and the 'step.call' entry in the stream handler map. step-host.test.ts builds its own IpcServer and handler maps instead, and the ac3 e2e test covers only a daemon without step.call. The only evidence for the production path is the three manual smoke checks of the installed daemon, recorded in S011/smoke.md (commit 284ce2c4). They are present as a record, not as runnable tests.

findings.message: The allowed target and size values are written out three times in this file: the inline union types in `oneShotRunParams`, the `AnalyzeOneShotArgs` interface, and the `TARGETS`/`SIZES` arrays used by `checkOneShotArgs`. Adding a value in one place but not the others would let the runtime check reject a value the types accept, or the reverse. Derive the types from the arrays (`(typeof TARGETS)[number]`) so there is one source.

`streamRequest` repeats the socket client's handling of stream frames: progress and delta go to `onFrame`, `done` resolves, an `error` frame becomes `ReviewStreamError('daemon-error', error, reason)`, and other frames are ignored. The parameter shaping for `workflow.review` and `codeReview.run` is repeated too. The shared types and reply helpers already live in `shared/review-stream.ts`, but the frame-to-failure mapping is now in two places, and the two clients could drift apart. That parity is guarded only by tests.

`waitText` rounds to the nearest minute, so a 90-second limit is reported as '2 minutes' (and the test asserts this). The timeout message 'no result from the daemon within 2 minutes' then overstates how long the wait actually lasted. This only affects the wording of the message.
